newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 11.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
FINANCIAL TIMES
POWER GROUPS PLAN FUND TO FIGHT LAW SUITS

Eight of the UK's main electricity companies, including National Grid, South Western Electricity and London Electricity, are to form an off-shore fighting fund to finance the legal battle against claims that electro-magnetic fields generated by high-tension power lines are hazardous to health.
The companies have been advised by insurance broker Willis Carroon to establish a company in Guernsey to fund what they see as being a "strenuous defence".
NATWEST ACQUIRES MERCHANT BANKING BOUTIQUE

NatWest Markets, the corporate finance subsidiary of National Westminster Bank, has acquired the merchant banking boutique Hambro Magan for an undisclosed sum. NatWest is understood to have beaten off interest from UBS, Commerzbank and Merrill Lynch to complete the purchase, which is thought to have cost in the region of 100 million stg. The deal fills the last important gap in the investment banking strategy of NatWest Markets.
INFLATION RISES IN WAKE OF STRONGER SPENDING

Official figures released Thursday from the Office for National Statistics reveal that the underlying rate of inflation rose unexpectedly in September, up to 2.9 per cent compared to 2.8 per cent in August. The small rise has further fuelled concern that the consumer spending recovery is stoking price pressures on the high street and that the chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, may not be able to keep price rises subdued in the run-up to the next election.
PENSION FUNDS FACE SHAKE-UP OVER 1.5 BLN STG VENTURE

British Telecommunications Pension Scheme (BTPS), the largest occupational fund in the UK, has announced a 1.5 billion stg joint venture with financial services and property group Liberty International. The new venture, Liberty International Pensions, will shake up UK pension fund management by undercutting traditional pensions providers and life assurers by offering lower costs and better service.
BRUSSELS RETREATS ON 40 PERCENT CUTS TO EU FISHING FLEETS

The European Commission has backtracked on plans to impose 40 percent cuts in the size of European Union fishing fleets after hostility from EU member states. EU Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino claimed there had been a "misunderstanding" about the commission's intentions, and that what it actually proposed was a 40 percent cut in catches, not fleet sizes. The issue is due to be discussed in what will be a stormy meeting of EU fisheries ministers next Monday.
ENVIRONMENT CHIEF URGES MORE TAKEOVERS

The chief executive of the Environment Agency has said that takeovers in the water industry should be encouraged. Speaking in an interview with the Financial Times newspaper, Ed Gallagher claimed that consolidation in the industry would help tackle water supply problems. The views contrast sharply with those of Ian Byatt, director general of industry regulator Ofwat.
-- BRITISH GAS ADMITS BILLING BLUNDERS

British Gas has publicly apologised to hundreds of customers in the south-west region after they received threatening letters demanding payment for bills they had not yet received. British Gas blamed "teething errors" with its new 150 million stg computerised billing system, introduced earlier this year. The company has spent an extra six million stg over the past few months to shore up the system.
VIRGIN ENTERS FRAY FOR AIR LIBERTE

Virgin Express, the low-cost European airline operated by Richard Branson's Virgin Group, is to battle with rivals British Airways over the remnants of French regional carrier Air Liberte. Air Liberte went into administration at the end of September, and British Airways is expected to submit a bid next week to administrators. Richard Branson has revealed that he has already been in talks with the administrators over the airline's assets and its landing and take-off slots in France.
BOOTS BACK ON INTERNATIONAL STAGE

UK-based retail chemist Boots is to return to the international stage with the opening of stores on a trial basis in Thailand, the Netherlands and Japan. It also plans to open a chain of outlets in the Republic of Ireland next month. The move is a second attempt at overseas expansion by Boots, which was forced to withdraw from an ill-fated Canadian venture in the late 1980s. The trial openings will cost the group 30 million stg over 18 months.
BASF JOINS SHELL AND HOECHST IN PLASTICS VENTURES

German chemicals company BASF has announced two joint ventures with Shell and Hoechst, as Europe's beleaguered plastics industry continues to consolidate. BASF is to merge its polypropylene business with that of Hoechst, and is also to undertake a 50:50 polyproplene joint venture with Shell. Profits in the plastics industry have been hit by volatile prices.
